rationale: The Latin anchors ire, venire, gradi, procedere, scandere all point to physical movement/locomotion (to go, to come, to walk, to proceed, to climb), and the OE verb a-stígan (lit. "to ascend/go up") is used in the attestations in a concrete sense of moving/travelling. The synset travel.v.01 ("change location; move, travel, or proceed") best captures this literal, physical sense of locomotion that underlies all the Latin glosses.
